title: Anderson localization in topological metals
abstract: We address the question of whether topological metals (TM) retain their nontrivial characteristics in the presence of disorder. While in the clean case, the issue is what protects the gaplessness of the spectrum, i.e. the band-touching nodes in TM, this question needs to be reformulated in the presence of disorder. The concept of gaplessness loses its sharp meaning in this case, since spectral gaps can be filled in by disorder-induced states. What is still meaningful is entanglement: one may ask whether the long-range entanglement of the clean gapless TM survives in the presence of disorder or, in other words, whether nontrivial topology protects the TM from Anderson localization. We demonstrate that such a protection exists in the case of three-dimensional (3D) Weyl semimetals, but not in 2D and 3D (type-I) Dirac or 3D nodal line semimetals. We establish this by combining the idea of unquantized anomaly as the topological response of TM with the decorated domain wall construction, used previously to discuss average symmetry-protected topological insulating phases.
summary: This theoretical work determines the robustness of topological protection in metals when disorder is introduced. It finds that only 3D Weyl semimetals maintain their nontrivial topological character against Anderson localization, while other semimetallic classes are susceptible to disorder-induced localization. The methodology relies on analyzing topological anomalies using advanced gauge field constructions.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the nontrivial topological characteristics of topological metals (TMs) survive when subjected to disorder, specifically addressing whether topology protects them from Anderson localization.
main_result: Protection against Anderson localization is demonstrated for 3D Weyl semimetals, but fails for 2D and 3D Dirac or nodal line semimetals, as their topological responses are compatible with localized states.
method: The analysis combines the concept of unquantized anomalies (a topological response) with the decorated domain wall construction, using gauge field formalisms derived from crystal plane phase functions.
model_or_system: The study focuses on various topological metals, including Weyl semimetals, Dirac semimetals, and nodal line semimetals, examining their behavior under random disorder potentials.
key_observables: Long-range entanglement, topological response coefficients ($\lambda$), and the failure of gauge invariance (anomaly) upon introducing vortices.
important_parameters: Dimensionality (2D vs 3D), symmetry protection (e.g., TR-invariance), and the degree of disorder realization.
main_assumptions: The concept of gaplessness loses meaning in disorder, requiring entanglement as the key diagnostic; the analysis assumes symmetry restoration on long length scales.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the topological response formalism using gauge fields, then applying this framework to analyze the stability of different classes of TMs (Weyl, Dirac, nodal line) under disorder, culminating in a comparative statement on which systems retain protection.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between topological invariants (anomalies) and localization physics provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding how fundamental symmetries dictate transport properties in disordered quantum materials, which is relevant to open quantum systems.
